newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bank says not affected by protests.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank says not affected by protests.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, said on Friday its business had not in any way been affected by nationwide protests across the sector against cuts by banks to work sick pay entitlements.
"There has been no effect at all on our business," a Deutsche spokesman said in response to an enquiry.

Banking and insurance trade union HBV had said earlier that business at Deutsche's branches in the northern town of Bremen had been "severely disrupted" as some of its employees joined an all-day strike involving a total 3,000 bank workers there.
Around 500 of Deutsche's employees had also staged walk-outs at its branches in the nearby port of Hamburg, union officials said.

The industrial action had been called to protest against a new law that has allowed employers to cut sick pay from 100 percent of salary to 80 percent. It follows mass protests last month in Germany's metal, engineering and chemical industries.

The Deutsche Bank spokesman said the bank continued to support the position of the banking employers federation in the dispute, which has advised banks that they are legally entitled to make the cuts.
